sections.title: Interview Answer
Mental Model
sections.content:
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    C[O(1): map lookup] --> L[O(log n): binary search]
    L --> N[O(n): linear scan]
    N --> NL[O(n log n): sort]
    NL --> N2[O(n²): nested loops]
    N2 --> E[O(2^n): naive recursion]
```

sections.title: Deep Dive
sections.content:
The formal definition, simply: f(n) is O(g(n)) if f(n) ≤ c·g(n) for large n — 'the growth rate is at most proportional to g(n).' The practical consequences:

Log n is the halving ladder: each step halves the problem — 1M elements in 20 steps, 1B in 30. This is why binary search on sorted data scales to any size.

The n-log-n floor for comparison sorting: any sort that only COMPARES elements (not radix/counting) has a proven lower bound of Ω(n log n) — the information-theoretic argument (n! orderings, each comparison distinguishes 2, so ≥ log2(n!) ≈ n log n).

The amortized concept: a map insertion is O(1) amortized — occasionally O(n) (the rehash), but averaged over n insertions, each is constant. The worst-single-op and the amortized cost are both honest numbers for different questions.

The interview discipline: name the complexity AND the reason (loop structure, halving pattern, hash function), then state the space cost. 'O(n) because single pass; O(n) space because we build a lookup map.' The reason matters more than the letter.
